title: Independent families: freely choosing sides and counting ultrafilters

based_on.title: Set Theory: The Third Millennium Edition, revised and expanded

summary: Continuum many subsets can realize every finite pattern of choices, giving the largest possible number of nonprincipal ultrafilters.
abstract: For finitely many subsets of the natural numbers, ask for a number that belongs to some specified sets and avoids the rest. An independent family leaves infinitely many answers to every such finite request, and can have as many members as there are real numbers. Assuming choice, any choice between each member and its complement can be extended to a nonprincipal ultrafilter, one containing no finite set. Different choices give different ultrafilters, so there are as many nonprincipal ultrafilters as there are families of subsets of the natural numbers.
